points: The second half of the chapter confronts false prophets like Achav ben Kolayah, Tzidkiyahu ben Maaseyah and Shemayah HaNechlami, who told the exiles they would be home soon. Yirmiyahu says they will die terribly.
Yirmiyahu writes to the exiles in Bavel: build houses, plant gardens, marry and have children and grandchildren. You'll be there 70 years. Judaism doesn't end outside the land.
"Seek the welfare of the city": we daven for the country we live in. Rabbi Jonathan Sacks shows this is the root of darkei shalom, caring for our non-Jewish neighbors while keeping our identity.
Hashem hears our tefillos anywhere. As the Kotzker Rebbe said, Hashem is wherever you let Him in, even in Bavel or Baltimore.

The Abarbanel: the second Bais Hamikdash was a lift to push us toward the full Geulah, and we missed it. The State of Israel is a similar lift, and we need to use it with more Torah, tefillah and tzedakah.
